name: The Cibao campos, Dominican Republic
region: Rural campos of the northern Cibao, from the Creighton-ILAC center in Santiago de los Caballeros

families.label: A farm family in a Cibao campo
families.leaveNote: No paid leave: 54.1% of Dominican workers are informal (Q1 2026). Paid maternity (14 weeks) reaches only the formal regime.
families.health: Covered by SENASA's subsidized plan, but specialists and surgery are in Santiago.

loanOptions.label: A prestamista (moneylender)
loanOptions.note: Prestamistas: about 20% a month, interest only (read with care).

loanOptions.label: Bank microcredit
loanOptions.note: Microcredit averaged 35.8% a year (Superintendencia de Bancos, March 2026).

loanOptions.label: Banco Agrícola, if they can reach it
loanOptions.note: Banco Agrícola lends at 8% (June 2025), if the family can reach it and has title.

families.lifeInsNote: Insurance of all kinds came to 1.4% of GDP, half the Latin American average (2022; read with care).

families.label: A Denver family with a salaried parent
families.leaveNote: Colorado FAMLI: up to 12 paid weeks; about 70% of pay at this salary (90% up to half the state average wage, 50% above).
families.health: Insured through work. Colorado's uninsured rate is 5.9% (2025).
families.loanNote: Average credit-card rate, 21.19% a year (Federal Reserve, Q3 2026).
families.lifeInsNote: 71% of U.S. households earning $150,000+ own life insurance (LIMRA 2024).

families.label: A Denver family whose father does day labor for cash
families.leaveNote: FAMLI needs $2,500 in reported Colorado wages; cash day labor often has none.
families.health: Coverage is uncertain; Denver Health is the city's safety net.
families.loanNote: Colorado caps small loans at 36% a year (Prop 111, 2018).
families.lifeInsNote: 31% of U.S. households earning under $50,000 own life insurance (LIMRA 2024).

shocks.label: A hurricane destroys the crop (hail totals the car here)

options.label: Banco Agrícola

options.label: A san (rotating savings)

FLOOR.title: Work with no floor: the campo and Denver
FLOOR.question: More than half of Dominican workers are informal. What does that take away, and what does a quintal of cacao pay by the hour?
FLOOR.guessIntro: For each item, guess whether the work comes with it. Then check, and compare with two Denver workers: one with a payslip and one paid in cash.

rates.text: of employed Dominicans were informal in early 2026, and 82.7% of the year's net new jobs were informal.
rates.src: Banco Central, ENCFT, via Revista Mercado, May 2026

rows.q: A minimum wage that applies to you

here.text: Outside a contract, the minimum wage doesn't reach you.
here.src: Banco Central, ENCFT, via Revista Mercado, May 2026

w2.text: $19.29 an hour in 2026, for anyone working in Denver, whatever their immigration status.

cash.text: The same law covers cash work, but 62% of 411 surveyed Denver-area day laborers had been cheated of wages.
cash.src: Galemba, University of Denver, 2016–17 (via Denver Labor)

here.text: A day you don't work is a day you aren't paid.
here.src: Banco Central, ENCFT, via Revista Mercado, May 2026

w2.text: 1 hour for every 30 worked, up to 48 hours a year, at every employer. It also covers a sick child and weather closures.
w2.src: CDLE, Healthy Families and Workplaces Act

cash.v: Only if the boss follows the law
cash.text: Denver Labor's 2025 cases included sick-pay violations.

rows.q: Paid time off after a new baby or a serious illness or injury

here.text: Paid leave runs through the social security system, and only for people who pay in.
here.src: Banco Central, ENCFT, via Revista Mercado, May 2026

w2.text: FAMLI: up to 12 weeks at about 90% of pay for lower earners, once you have $2,500 in reported Colorado wages.

cash.text: FAMLI runs on reported wages. Cash pay doesn't count.

rows.q: Pay while you look for work if the job ends

here.src: Banco Central, ENCFT, via Revista Mercado, May 2026

w2.text: Unemployment insurance, based on reported wages.
w2.src: our reading of the eligibility rules (Denver mirror)

cash.src: our reading of the eligibility rules (Denver mirror)

rows.q: Credit toward a pension in old age

here.text: No contributions to the social security system, no pension from work.
here.src: Banco Central, ENCFT, via Revista Mercado, May 2026

w2.text: Every reported paycheck builds Social Security credits.
w2.src: our reading of the eligibility rules (Denver mirror)

cash.src: our reading of the eligibility rules (Denver mirror)

rows.q: Health care that comes with the work

here.text: Not through work. A subsidized public plan covers families on the poverty register, but it is paid far less per person than the workers' plan.

w2.text: Many low-wage jobs offer none. Health First Colorado covers adults up to 133% of the poverty level whatever their job.

cash.text: The same income-based coverage is open to them.

rows.q: A pay record a bank or landlord will accept

here.text: No payslip, so no bank loan or formal lease on that income.
here.src: Banco Central, ENCFT, via Revista Mercado, May 2026

w2.text: A payslip and a tax record.
w2.src: our reading of the eligibility rules (Denver mirror)

cash.src: our reading of the eligibility rules (Denver mirror)

rows.q: An office that will come if you are cheated

here.text: A painter paid for four days of five has no office to call.

w2.text: Denver Labor recovered a record $2.31 million for about 7,200 workers in 2025.

cash.text: The office covers anyone working in Denver, but fewer than 40% of cheated day laborers asked for help.
cash.src: Galemba, University of Denver, 2016–17 (via Denver Labor)

grid.after: Informal doesn't mean illegal or lazy. It means work that the protections were never built to reach: social insurance, paid sick days, paid leave. Denver has informal work too. The difference is how much of all the work it is.

piece.minText: the field workers' minimum, RD$714.60 for an 8-hour day
piece.intro: A cacao grower learns the price on the day of sale. Turn a quintal into hours of work.

options.label: Farm-gate price, May 2026
options.text: RD$7,000–8,000 a quintal; this uses the middle (our arithmetic).

options.label: Farm-gate price, a year earlier
options.text: RD$20,000–30,000 a quintal; this uses the middle (our arithmetic).

pace.label: Hours of work for one quintal (your estimate)
pace.note: Pruning, harvest, fermenting and drying, over a season. No source gives it. Set your own, and leave out what the inputs cost.

piece.after: Work paid by the piece is counted in pieces and prices, never in hours. The hours disappear, and so does the comparison with a wage.

den.src: CDLE, Healthy Families and Workplaces Act

month.denNote: Paid sick leave (48 hours a year) covers your own illness, a child's, and weather closures. FAMLI covers a longer illness or injury once you have $2,500 in reported wages. Both need a payslip; cash work gets neither in practice.

pay.text: The lowest legal monthly minimum (micro firms), RD$16,993.20 from Feb 2026. What informal campo work pays is not published, so set your own.

month.intro: Pay comes by the day. Pick what happens this month and see who still gets paid.

events.label: Slow week: half the usual sales (3 days)
events.w2: a payslip job can cut hours too, so this is unpaid

events.label: A buyer or boss doesn't pay (1 day)
events.w2: unpaid unless a claim with Denver Labor recovers it

doing.text: Neighbors work each other's land or roof in turn; rotating savings groups (san) pay out one pot a round; the colmado gives credit (fiao) until payday.

FLOOR.notice: Switch the year. The same quintal, grown the same way, paid more than three times as much in hours one year as the next. A grower who signed a contract before a spike kept none of it.
FLOOR.yourCall: If you grew cacao, would you sign a contract at a fixed price? What would you gain, and what would you give up?

HOURS.title: What the pay has to cover: the campo and Denver
HOURS.question: What share of a month's pay does the basic basket for the lowest-income households take? Compare it with Denver.
HOURS.notice: The basket here is the Banco Central's own measure for the poorest fifth of households, and it already includes more than food. One field worker at the legal minimum covers less than two-thirds of it.
HOURS.yourCall: What fills the gap: a second earner, money from New York or Madrid, or credit at the colmado? What does each one cost?

pays.label: The field workers' minimum (26 days)
pays.note: RD$714.60 for an 8-hour day, × 26 days (our arithmetic).

pays.label: The micro-firm minimum wage
pays.note: RD$16,993.20 a month from Feb 2026, the lowest legal monthly minimum.

pays.label: Set it yourself
pays.note: Informal campo pay isn't published. Set your own and say so.

food.lab: Basic basket, lowest-income fifth of households
food.text: Banco Central: RD$29,489.84 a month for a household in the lowest-income fifth, food and other needs (May 2026).

pays.label: The minimum wage (one full-time earner)
pays.note: $19.29 an hour in 2026, about $3,343 a month full time (our arithmetic).

pays.label: Set it yourself
pays.note: Day labor and cash work often pay less: 62% of surveyed Denver-area day laborers had experienced wage theft (2016–17).

food.text: USDA Thrifty Food Plan: $1,018.20 a month for a family of four (June 2026), about $255 a person (our arithmetic). National, not Denver prices.
food.src: USDA Thrifty Food Plan via WTOP

rent.text: Denver metro median rent: $1,874 a month, all units (ACS 2020–2024).

bus.text: RTD standard fare: $2.75 for a three-hour pass.
